Reads one number of the last measured frame, in milliseconds, by its key. A frame is the time from one [Flip](Flip) to the next, and the numbers are updated by every Flip, so reading them right after a Flip gives the frame that just ended and nothing needs to be parsed. The key is the name of the item, in any case: `frame` (the time of the whole frame), the timers of the runtime (`UpdateWorld`, `animation`, `RenderWorld`, `EntityInView`, `CopyRect`, `Flip`, `Delay`, `RenderWorld: lights+cameras`, `RenderWorld: collect`, `RenderWorld: draws`, `RenderWorld: sort+group`, `clusters for GPU culling`, `record commands`), `waiting for the GPU`, the GPU passes (`gpu scene`, `gpu 2d`, `gpu copy`, `gpu present`, `gpu frame`) and `vkQueueSubmit`, followed by the keys of the program's own parts ([ProfileSectionStart](ProfileSectionStart)). [ProfileItemName](ProfileItemName) lists the keys. The GPU times come back a frame or two late, so they are what finished during that frame. Without `--profile` (or `-d`), or with the timers off ([ProfileEnable](ProfileEnable)), the numbers stay 0.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 64, 64, 0, 2
For i = 1 To 10
	Cls
	Flip
	Print "frame " + ProfileFlipCount() + ": " + ProfileValue("frame") + " ms, draws " + ProfileValue("RenderWorld: draws")
Next
```
@param key  The name of the item, such as `frame` or `RenderWorld: draws`.
@returns The time in milliseconds, 0 for a key that does not exist.
@gap This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command.
